title: Nat.RM.self_halting_not_decidable: no total decider is correct about its own self-referential halting
statement: The machine model (nat_prelude/computability.rs, ADR-1611): a 'program' is a step function step : Nat -> Nat on a Nat-encoded configuration space; runFuel step c fuel iterates step fuel times from c (structural recursion on fuel alone); Halts step x := exists fuel, runFuel step x fuel = 0 (0 is the halted state). diagStep H c := if H c then c else 0 is the machine built from a candidate decider H : Nat -> Bool that asks H about its OWN current configuration at every step. This theorem: assume H is correct in BOTH directions about whether diagStep H halts from the fixed marker input 1 (Eq Bool (H 1) true -> Halts (diagStep H) 1, and conversely) -- then False. WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT CLAIM (read before citing): H is assumed correct ONLY at the single point 1, for the single machine diagStep H -- narrower than 'H decides Halts for every step function at every input', because the proof never uses more. This is a genuine constructive refutation (the two correctness directions plus diagStep's definition are jointly inconsistent, axiom-free, no excluded middle) but it is NOT Turing's theorem for a fixed Turing-complete universal machine: there is no program-as-data encoding, no s-m-n theorem, no recursion theorem, and Halts is not shown undecidable for an ENUMERATION of machines -- only for the one self-referential instance a candidate H itself determines. The proof is built from the same technique Nat.cantor_no_fixed_point's family uses (a Bool.rec/Or case split closed by Bool/Nat disjointness facts, not excluded middle) but does NOT literally call that declared theorem -- ADR-1611 records the attempt to route through it directly and why the two proof cases (one needing a fuel-induction non-halting fact, the other needing only one step) close more directly through Nat.succ_ne_zero and Bool.true_ne_false respectively.

formal.statement: theorem Nat.RM.self_halting_not_decidable : ((x0 : ((x0 : AxNat) -> Bool)) -> ((x1 : ((x1 : Eq.{1} Bool (x0 (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) Bool.true) -> AxNat.RM.Halts (AxNat.RM.diagStep x0) (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero))) -> ((x2 : ((x2 : AxNat.RM.Halts (AxNat.RM.diagStep x0) (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) -> Eq.{1} Bool (x0 (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) Bool.true)) -> False)))

evidence.supports: Nat.RM.self_halting_not_decidable is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example kernel_declaration_projection -- --require-declaration Nat.RM.self_halting_not_decidable --require-kind theorem
evidence.notes: --require-declaration exits non-zero when the name is absent from every constructed prelude, and --require-kind exits non-zero when it is present with the wrong kind, so the exit status depends on the finding rather than on the run completing. --release is MANDATORY: this binary builds creal/complex/cpoint, which overflow the default debug thread stack. formal.statement is the SAME binary's unfiltered emit's rendered-type column, verbatim -- confirmed identical across all nine constructed preludes (nat/list/integer/characterization/rat/creal/complex/cpoint/metric/ipc), since the Nat prelude's own construction does not vary by which OTHER preludes are built alongside it.

The per-declaration figure (0) is pinned separately by computability_tests.rs::self_halting_not_decidable_is_a_declared_axiom_free_theorem, which also asserts the declaration IS a Declaration::Theorem (not silently a Definition or Axiom) -- run via: cargo test -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --lib self_halting_not_decidable_is_a_declared_axiom_free_theorem -- --test-threads=4 2>&1 | grep -cE '^test result: ok\. 1 passed'.

evidence.supports: The machine model's DEFINITIONS (diagStep/runFuel), which the theorem's soundness rests on, evaluate correctly: diagStep self-loops under a constant-true decider and halts in one step under a constant-false decider, each pinned by def_eq at concrete numerals against a negative control naming the swapped (wrong) value.
evidence.checker_command: cargo test -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --lib nat_prelude::computability_tests -- --test-threads=4 2>&1 | grep -cE '^test result: ok\. 5 passed'
evidence.notes: A Definition's kind-check (well-typed) cannot see a wrong VALUE -- Nat -> Nat -> Nat is Nat -> Nat -> Nat whatever it computes. Four of the five tests reduce diagStep/runFuel at concrete small numerals (1, 5, 9; fuel 0..5) against hand-computed values with a negative control naming the specific swapped case_true/case_false or mis-ordered succ-case value; the fifth confirms the theorem itself is a declared, axiom-free Theorem. grep -c rather than grep -q, which would SIGPIPE the producer under pipefail; anchored with [[:space:]]-free literals, never \t.

No type was hand-transcribed. Prose is hand-written; see ADR-1611 for the full design rationale and the rejected/deferred alternatives (an explicit register-machine front end; Nat.Partrec.Code).

notes: Read the scope boundary in `statement` before citing this as 'the halting problem is undecidable' without qualification -- it is a genuine, narrower, constructive result about ONE self-referential instance, not Turing's theorem for a fixed universal machine over an enumeration of programs. ADR-1611 names the natural next step (Nat.Primrec's sibling Nat.Partrec.Code, reusing the already-built Nat.pair/unpairLeft/unpairRight) that would close that gap. The undecidability of first-order validity, named alongside this in docs/math-department/10-logic-and-foundations.md, was NOT attempted and stays `open` in this ledger with nothing behind it.
